deepdive.sec: Financial Services — Small Finance Bank (microfinance-origin; JLG→individual-loan transition plus a secured retail build-out in commercial vehicles and mortgages)

bull_bear.body:
- **CRAR 20%**, target band **20-22%** — "in terms of our capital adequacy from where it stands today, we will increase it marginally. But yes, I mean 20% to 22% is where we would ideally want to be given the kind of growth that we are having."
- **Tier 2: an existing tranche expires next year; the bank is in the market now** — "we are out in the market, evaluating our proposals for raising fresh Tier 2. We hope all things going well. We hope to close something this quarter."
- **Tier 1: enabling resolution going to the AGM, nothing decided** — "We are evaluating at this particular point in time in terms of what would be the right time to raise Tier 1. Nothing finalized as of now."
- **Funding stack diversification** as capital-efficiency: IBPC re-opened at sub-5%, refinance lines available, PSLC monetisation of the priority-sector surplus (₹1,600cr sold this quarter).
- **No buyback, dividend or acquisition discussed on this call.**
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body:
1. **The 1.6% Q1 ROA is PSLC-flattered.** ₹40-46cr of PSL income against a ₹75cr/quarter PAT run-rate ambition; guided PSLC drops to ₹10-15cr in Q2/Q3. Management pre-warned Q2 will be "a little subdued". The ₹300cr+ FY27 PAT guide therefore requires the paying-book growth and CLOU income to backfill ~₹25-30cr per quarter.
2. **The PSLC number was given three different ways on one call** (₹90-odd cr / ₹46cr / ₹40cr). Reconcile against the investor presentation before modelling.
3. **The CGFMU-adjusted GNPA/NNPA bridge (6.5%→2.9%, 1.2%→0.3%) was not explained** and does not follow from the ₹134cr receivable alone. Reported 6.5% GNPA is the number that stands unqualified.
4. **CGFMU claims are close to exhausted as an earnings support** — ₹15-20cr left this FY, ₹135-150cr only in later years, against ₹387cr recognised this quarter.
5. **Systemic CGFMU/NCGTC capacity risk if the industry crowds in** — the analyst's question was pointed and management did not fully answer it: "I wouldn't be really able to comment in terms of overall, but the NCGTC as a corporation is very well funded." MD's own framing is a hedge: "maybe the premium we'll pay in the next couple of years, maybe will be higher than the claims that we'll make."
6. **Vehicle-finance PAR rose 10.1% → 11.5%** on fuel prices and Middle-East-driven load availability, with monsoon seasonality still ahead. Management expects recovery "around September" — a Q3, not Q2, fix.
7. **Mortgage slippages requiring legal resolution** — small in count ("a couple") but a new stress location in the very segment being scaled.
8. **Deposits are the binding constraint on 30% growth.** MD: "Deposits will -- may look like a challenge… It will be challenging, and we'll have to very armor ourselves to ensure that." FD rates "have not really come down". Holding CASA at 21% requires ~20% CASA growth on its own arithmetic.
9. **Yield reset is structural, not cyclical** — secured mix rising at ~12% yield vs VL at ~25%. The guided return to 17%+ depends on MFI NPL recoveries normalising, which is exactly what weakened this quarter.
10. **Tier 2 expiry next year with the refi not yet closed** — "we hope to close something this quarter" is the only capital action with a date on it.
11. **Management's own caution on reading the MFI turn as an all-clear:** "It is extremely important that we do not really take this as a reveal of the cycle and go aggressive."
12. **Competitive intensity in the SFB/MFI space** explicitly flagged: "The competition will be intense and that is where probably our digital play will be coming to play."
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body:
Confident but deliberately unheroic — the defining feature of this call is management **talking down** a beat. Having printed the Q4-target ROA in Q1, the CFO immediately capped the extrapolation ("We need to be cognizant of the fact that we had INR40 crores of PSL income"), and the MD refused to raise ROE guidance: "We are not really to kind of guiding higher ROE at this point of time… It may not necessarily happen Q2 will better than Q1 and so on, consistently across parameters." The framing throughout is sustainability over slope — "can every improvement be sustainable quarter-on-quarter?" — with a stated visibility horizon of "4 to 6 quarters."

Disclosure quality is mixed. The operating detail is genuinely granular (customer grading distribution targets, cohort benchmarking, CLOU funnel conversion, SA vs FD cost split, officer-productivity math), and the CGFMU answer to a hostile systemic question was candid rather than promotional — including the admission that credit insurance "is going to be our license to do business" and that premiums may exceed claims. Against that: **NII and NIM were never quantified**, the PSLC number moved three times, the adjusted-NPA bridge was left unexplained, an ROE answer came out in ROA units, and the opex "67% to 70%" was given without a stated denominator. The CEO's answers are discursive and occasionally hard to parse verbatim.

Notably, the MD's insurance philosophy is a genuine differentiator in tone: "We are not looking at it as a shield for doing business… Whatever insurance we are taking it as the kind of the last resort. If you had to do yourself, will be a business model able to sustain during that down cycle of 1 year, 1.5 years. That's the way we are looking at it."
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body:
- **The CGFMU claim is a cash event, not an accounting one, and it has already re-rated the funding side.** The IBPC market re-opened at sub-5% *because* the MFI book cleaned up — "with the improvement in the MFI book, the IBPC market has opened up for us again". Insurance recovery → clean book → cheaper marginal funding is the actual transmission chain, and it is worth more than the ₹387cr itself.
- **Assets are now growing faster than deposits, and management calls that a *good* sign** — "assets have started growing at a faster pace as compared to the deposits, which is a good sign. So there's a demand in the market for loans." That is an unusual thing for a bank at 21% CASA to celebrate, and it is why deposits are named the constraint later in the same call.
- **The through-cycle number management actually believes:** "even in the entire cycle, what we saw, is that 75% to 80% of the customers continue to be very good, including in the cycle, it is at 20%." The whole A/B/C/D/E grading apparatus exists to keep that 20% off the book — a 2-SD/3-SD scenario is sized at "around 12%, 14% portfolio kind of at risk".
- **CLOU's economics are deliberately un-modellable and that is the point** — a sub-₹5,000 average ticket that "gets extinguished at the end of the month and the remit starts again". It is being run for the customer graph and the VKYC rail, with the explicit intent to build "other digital products and even probably other secured asset products" on top.
- **"Both own the customer."** The MD's answer on Paytm partnership economics is a rejection of the usual ownership framing: "none of the customers have a single relationship, they have a relationship with multi-financial service providers. So whoever provides best of customer experience and product feature for that particular product tends to kind of win." Read as a signal that Suryoday will multi-home its CLOU distribution rather than defend exclusivity.
- **The JLG exit is now a branch-design decision, not a portfolio-runoff decision** — "Even in the new branches where we are opening up our focus now starts with NTBVL and VL rather than getting customers with JLG." The graduation pipeline that defined the SFB model has been cut at the source.
- **VL is being segmented into 6-7 sub-cohorts with target ratios per cohort** — a level of intra-product stratification not yet visible in the disclosed reporting, and the mechanism by which management intends to avoid the next cycle without raising ticket sizes ("not increasing our ticket raises in VL").
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

business.body:
**Inclusive Finance (the backbone; 44% of advances, down from 48%)**
- Strategic shift from JLG to individual loans (Vikas Loan / VL, and **new-to-bank NTB-VL**): "individual loans contribute around 80% of our monthly onboarding" and the JLG book is to shrink over the next 1-1.5 years. New branches now open *starting* with NTB-VL/VL rather than routing customers through the JLG pipe.
- MFI paying book grew "by about INR500-odd crores in one quarter"; MD separately cites the IF paying book "growing at least INR120 crores, INR150 crores".
- Underwriting overhaul since **November 2024**: beyond the standard 2-lender/3-lender filters, the bank added the unsecured-loan basket, recency of unsecured loans, a "heating factor" on unsecured loans, and payment behaviour → customers graded **A/B/C/D/E**, lending focused on A/B/C ("In a good market, we can do more C and D. But at the moment, market also gets tougher, then we focus more and more on A and B"), tested across three time-frame cohorts. Target composition: "minimum 40% in category A, 30% in category B."
- The same profiling now covers **micro-banking including MSME and individual loans**.

**Secured retail — Commercial Vehicles (incl. construction equipment)**
- **75-80% of the CV book is used CV**, deliberately: "we focus more on used business, where the ticket sizes are much lower than compared to the new vehicles."
- **PAR 11.5% vs 10.1% QoQ.** Stated causes: "the fuel prices increase and also in terms of load availability due to the crisis in Middle East", plus normal monsoon seasonality — "in the second quarter across the country when you have monsoon activated, the PAR is generally slightly elevated. But this being an earning asset, it goes back early around September."
- No geographic concentration: "We are spread across Southwest and Northern markets."
- Benchmarking claim: "if we benchmark as a 1-year portfolio, 2-year portfolio, 3-year cohort portfolio, we are significantly outperformed the market by 2x, 2.5x on the credit quality."
- Focus shifting toward **light and small commercial vehicles**.

**Secured retail — Mortgages / micro-mortgages**
- Present in "no more than 25% of our current branches"; intent 40-45% by year-end. Micro-mortgages named as the key product-gap fill.
- **Slippage pocket this quarter:** "We have had a couple of slippages in our mortgage business and which we are working on for resolution through legal process… we are well collateralized. The collaterals are well identified and quite liquid in the market. So we will try to complete the resolution process in the coming quarter."

**Digital / CLOU**
- Convenience fee income **₹18cr**, cost **₹13cr**, both gross-up items. Partner: **Paytm** — "our current partner is Paytm. They'll be expanding their kind of the partnership… but we'll also be kind of onboarding a few more partners."
- Digital MSME disbursements **₹59cr**; digital deposits **₹2,222cr** at ~**₹6cr/day** accretion; secured credit cards and digital deposits named as the other digital rails.

**Liabilities**
- Retail deposits **87.3%**; CASA ratio **21%**, with the SA-first push ("We are currently focusing more on SA. Over time, we will also start focusing on our current account product features"). Selective on bulk. Preferred tenor: "anywhere between 2, 2.5 year FD money". Retail ticket "on average of around less than INR2 lakhs per customer".
business.title: Segment / subsidiary detail

business.body:
- **CGFMU coverage of a largely-covered inclusive-finance book, taken out *before* the cycle turned** — and it converted to cash. MD: "if you look at it when the going was good is when we said that we will cover our portfolio. And obviously we thought that as a pure insurance, but it has certainly protected the balance sheet on the capital." Evidence: **₹387cr received in Q1 FY27**; NNPA down to ₹170cr / 1.2%.
- **A three-cohort-validated proprietary borrower segmentation** running since Nov-2024, layering unsecured-loan recency/"heating factor"/payment behaviour on top of the industry-standard lender-count filters: "we tested it for 3 different time frames cohorts, and it's holding good."
- **Used-CV credit quality benchmarked at 2-2.5x the market** on 1/2/3-year cohorts (management's own claim, unquantified beyond the multiple).
- **Self-service collection behaviour:** ~70% of customers pay without any officer contact — the structural cost advantage behind the officer-productivity plan.

business.title: Challenges → beneficiaries & losers (listed names)

latest_quarter.body:
- **Yield fell 17.2% → 16.1% on non-NPA advances**, decomposed by the CFO into (a) IF share down 4pts, 48%→44%, worth "about a INR0.75 impact", and (b) a weaker MFI-recovery-led income recognition vs a strong Q4. Guided back to ~17%, stabilized band 17.2-17.5%, with secured yield ~12% and VL ~25-25.25% as the mix bookends.
- **Funding: cost of funds down ~8bps QoQ**, but the relief is coming from savings-account repricing, not term deposits — "We continue to see a pressure in the rates for fixed deposits. They have not really come down. What we have done as a bank is that we have optimized our rates in the savings account across bucket." SA 5.7%→5.5%; FD ~8.1%. IBPC at sub-5% is the cheapest marginal rupee available.
- **NIM guided flat**, no number disclosed. Given the yield reset down and the CoF guide of ~7.5%, the Q2 NIM print is the single most important verification item from this call.
- **Opex 67-70% "full stack"**, absorbing technology, branch expansion and branch personnel.
- **CLOU grosses up both sides of the P&L** — ₹18cr income vs ₹13cr cost; as it scales "you'll see a proportionate increase in the other income and other expense as well" (confirmed: "Absolutely correct").
- **No pricing action planned**, despite the yield reset — customer stratification, not price, is the lever: "We have a single price that is offered across but our customer stratification has increased."
latest_quarter.title: Margins & cost dynamics

latest_quarter.body:
- **Q1 FY27 (this):** Gross advances ₹14,376cr (+32.5% YoY); deposits ₹14,634cr (+29.4% YoY), retail 87.3%, CASA ratio 21%. **₹387cr CGFMU claims received in the quarter** (₹386cr per opening remarks) — GNPA 6.5% / ₹931cr, NNPA 1.2% / ₹170cr, of which ₹134cr CGFMU-receivable; management's CGFMU-adjusted basis 2.9% / 0.3% (bridge unexplained). PCR "above 80%" — analyst-stated, unchallenged; no PCR figure from management. Slippages: bank ₹92cr (from ₹106cr), MFI ₹53cr (from ₹73cr), MFI <₹20cr/month. Credit cost 0.8% (guide 0.8-1.00%). Collection efficiency: IF current bucket 99.2%, recent-portfolio current bucket 99.4%, run-rate "stabilizing at 99.3%, 99.5%". **ROA 1.6% achieved in Q1 vs 1.6% guided for Q4** — but flattered by PSLC (₹1,600cr certificates sold; income variously stated ₹90-odd cr / ₹46cr / ₹40cr). Other income ~₹147cr. Yield on non-NPA advances 17.2% → 16.1% (IF share 48% → 44%); guide back to 17%, band 17.2-17.5%. CoF −~8bps QoQ, guide ~7.5%; SA 5.7% → 5.5%, FD ~8.1%; IBPC re-opened at sub-5%. **NII and NIM not disclosed on this call.** CLOU: fee ₹18cr / cost ₹13cr, ~6 lakh users (9-10 lakh approved), Paytm partner, guide to ~12 lakh users this FY. Vehicle PAR 11.5% (from 10.1%) on fuel + Middle-East load availability. CRAR 20% (target 20-22%); **fresh Tier 2 "hope to close something this quarter"**; Tier 1 resolution to AGM, nothing finalized. FY27 PAT guide ₹300cr+ / ~₹75cr per quarter held, Q2 pre-warned "a little subdued". ~50 branches over Q2+Q3; mortgage branch coverage ≤25% → 40-45% by FY27-end. Residual CGFMU claims ₹15-20cr this FY, ₹135-150cr later.
- _Q2 FY27 → check: **(1) NIM and NII finally disclosed** and whether NIM held at the (undisclosed) Q1 level against the 16.1% yield and ~7.5% CoF guide; (2) PAT ≥ ~₹75cr despite PSLC dropping to ₹10-15cr — i.e. did the paying book + CLOU backfill ~₹25-30cr; (3) **which PSLC number the presentation confirms** (₹90/₹46/₹40cr); (4) the CGFMU-adjusted GNPA bridge explained, and reported GNPA direction from 6.5%; (5) **Tier 2 raise actually closed in Q2** as guided, and any Tier 1 movement post-AGM; (6) vehicle PAR from 11.5% — management expects recovery only "around September", so Q2 may worsen before Q3 improves; (7) the "couple of" mortgage slippages resolved through legal process "in the coming quarter"; (8) branch adds tracking to ~50 across Q2+Q3 and mortgage coverage moving off 25%; (9) CASA held at 21% while deposits grow ~20-30% — management's own named challenge; (10) IF share of advances vs the 48:52 micro-banking mix target, and whether it fell further below 44%; (11) CLOU users vs the ~12 lakh exit-FY27 target and any new distribution partner beyond Paytm; (12) collection efficiency vs the 99.3-99.5% stabilisation band through the monsoon._
latest_quarter.title: QoQ change log (fill each quarter)

outlook.body:
- **PAT: ₹300cr+ for FY27, reaffirmed.** Asked directly whether there is "any risk you see to your guidance of INR300 crores plus PAT for this financial year", MD: "As of now, no, we are kind of in a very focus in term of INR75 crores per quarter is what we are looking at. Maybe Q2 will be a little subdued because we said that we had in terms of the PSL income."
- **ROA: 1.6% by Q4 FY27 — unchanged.** "we maintain the guidance for fourth quarter 1.6% kind of ROA" → "There is no change in the guidance from what we had indicated at the start of the year." *Already achieved in Q1.*
- **ROE: "1.3% to 1.4%"** (CFO, in answer to a **steady-state ROE** question — the units appear to be a misspeak; MD later frames the same range as "we end up 13% to 14%"). **Both statements recorded as spoken.** MD's ambition: "we can really inch it up by meaningful and sustainable 0.5% to 1% in terms of ROE year-on-year for the next couple of years."
- **Credit cost: 0.8-1.00% for FY27** — "like we had indicated at the start of the year, our guidance is that we will be somewhere between to 0.8 to 1.00%, and we stay by that guidance." Q1 print 0.8%.
- **Cost of funds: ~7.5% for the rest of the year** — "You can expect the cost of fund to be at around 7.5% for the rest of the year." MD adds: "intend is to really keep the cost of funds around at the same level certainly for Q2 and Q3."
- **NIM: stable at the Q1 level** — asked "do you expect the NIMs to be stable at the current level?", CFO: "Yes, yes, very similar to what we are having at the end of Q1." *No NIM figure was given on the call.*
- **Yield on advances: back to ~17%; stabilized range 17.2-17.5%** — "we will be going back to around 17%"; IR head: "stabilized yield on advances would be 17.2% to 17.5% because our secured asset also, our yield is nearly 12%."
- **Pricing: no change in the near term** — "At this particular point in time, we don't foresee an immediate change in pricing across products… in this quarter, we don't quite foresee us changing our price."
- **PSLC income: ₹10-15cr in each of Q2 and Q3, ~₹15-20cr in Q4.**
- **Opex: 67-70%** ("the kind of target that we have assumed for ourselves to be in the range of around 67% to 70%. This is a full stack cost, including our investments in technology, branch expansion, branch-led personnel and all of that together"). *Basis (cost-to-income vs cost-to-assets) was not specified on the call.*
- **Growth: ~30%, with deposits the binding constraint.** MD: "That's 30% growth, including probably 20% growth to maintain the CASA ratio even at 21%. It will be challenging." Analyst framing of "30%, 35% as you have guided in FY27" went unchallenged. Retail secured businesses "have been growing anywhere between 30% to 35% on a year-on-year basis."
- **Mix: micro-banking to be held at a 48:52 mix** — "we would like to keep to a 48, 52 kind of a mix… that's the kind of a mix that we would continue to have."
- **Individual-loan migration: ~80% of monthly onboarding already; JLG exposure to be reduced "over a period of next 1 year, 1.5 years."**
- **Capital: CRAR 20%, target 20-22%. Fresh Tier 2 — "We hope to close something this quarter."** Tier 1: "we have a resolution going into the AGM… Nothing finalized as of now."
- **Branches: "closer to 50 branches in this quarter and next quarter"**, weighted to inclusive finance and commercial vehicles. **Mortgage coverage from "no more than 25% of our current branches" to "at least 40% to 45% towards the end of the year."**
- **CGFMU claims: ₹15-20cr residual this FY; a further ₹135-150cr claimable "not this year, but subsequently".**
- **CLOU users: double from ~6 lakh to ~12 lakh during this financial year** — "we will be comfortable if we are able to achieve double the customer count during this financial year from closer to 6 lakh users probably to around 12 lakh users. That is a conservative number."

Not applicable in the classic sense (bank). The forward-flow equivalents disclosed on the call:
- **CLOU approval funnel:** ~6 lakh customers utilising, **9-10 lakh approved**, onboarding **1.5-2 lakh customers per month**, "assuming that around 70% - 60% gets approved at around 1.5 lakh and around 1 lakh when we start placing it". Scaling "closer to probably 5%, 10% on a month-on-month basis". Average ticket **less than ₹5,000**, "very, very small EMI product. It gets extinguished at the end of the month and the remit starts again."
- **Prequalified digital base:** "phygital customer base acquired through digital deposits and other digital products stands at approximately 1 million customers having a good credit record."
- **Credit-on-UPI customers crossed 9 lakhs**, onboarded via VKYC.
- **CGFMU claim pipeline:** ₹15-20cr residual in FY27; **₹135-150cr claimable in later years** "as things stand today".
- **Funding pipeline:** IBPC market "has opened up for us again" post MFI improvement — one IBPC taken at "around 5%, a little less than 5%"; refinance lines to be tapped "as and when required".
outlook.title: Order book & pipeline

outlook.body:
- **CLOU as a customer-acquisition engine, not a lending P&L:** "the potential on this considering it is a small ticket and instantaneous, and it gives us a large base on which we have to build other digital products and even probably other secured asset products." Target: double users to ~12 lakh this FY, described as conservative; VKYC capacity to be scaled "for doubling or tripling".
- **Multi-partner CLOU distribution** beyond Paytm — explicitly on the table.
- **Micro-mortgages + CV into existing branches** — the cheapest growth lever available: "not all our products are available in all our present locations… we have a large opportunity in terms of expanding to existing locations and branches in the retail secured products."
- **IBPC as a re-opened funding market** — a direct consequence of MFI book quality improving: "with the improvement in the MFI book, the IBPC market has opened up for us again… with the improvement in the MFI book, the funding options only increase."
- **Productivity optionality in the IL model:** relationship-officer capacity to move from "only 400, 500" customers (JLG norm) to "600, 700 and probably more", because "closer to 70% of the customer as we see today, are making that payment without reaching out to them" — via WhatsApp, branch or digital, before the 7th-of-month due date.

deepdive.thesis: Suryoday's Q1 FY27 is the quarter the CGFMU insurance thesis actually paid out in cash: **₹387cr of claims received in the quarter** (₹386cr in the opening remarks) took net NPA to ₹170cr / 1.2%, and management pulled the full-year ROA target forward — the 1.6% that was guided for *Q4* FY27 was already printed in *Q1*. Underneath, the mix is shifting fast — inclusive-finance share of advances fell 48%→44%, individual loans are ~80% of monthly onboarding, and the CLOU (credit-line-on-UPI, Paytm) book is compounding 5-10% month-on-month — while gross advances grew 32.5% YoY to ₹14,376cr against deposits +29.4% to ₹14,634cr. The catch is that the print is flattered by a one-off: **~₹46cr of PSLC income from ₹1,600cr of certificates sold**, which the CFO says drops to ₹10-15cr per quarter for the next two quarters, so Q2 is guided to be "a little subdued" even as the ₹300cr+ FY27 PAT guidance is held.
